ops.entry: WHEN re-reviewing a fix meant to close a defect class DO map the contract's distinct states across phase changes, probe the exception families the guard excludes, and test one reachable case beyond the boundary. A passing replay of the original failure closes that instance, not the class.
ops.why: Replaces a broad omission prompt with a concrete action for class closure: the closed object, buffered shutdown, and missing-at-exec cases survived different instance fixes.

ops.entry: WHEN reporting a finding adjacent to a terminal closure class DO separate its consequence from class membership. Name the triggering state and its reachability, whether the faulting line changed, and what identical input does at base. Route the evidence to the ruling tier rather than requesting another fix round.
ops.why: Displaces generic defect-class labeling with the facts that settled the final dispute: healthy streams, an opt-in trigger, an unchanged source line, and a less harmful pinned outcome.

ops.entry: WHEN a CLI exit-status claim depends on buffering or shutdown DO measure the real child through termination with interpreter flags and relevant environment explicit. Remove inherited overrides to establish the default case, then measure supported overrides separately; an unbuffered green run cannot establish buffered shutdown behavior.
ops.why: Buffered and unbuffered children exited differently after the same write. This replaces a deletion-sweep reminder already covered by the retained sweep patterns.

originals.original: WHEN evaluating a boundary or identity check against an enumerated set of adversarial questions — your own or an inherited peer's clearance — DO ask what category the set omits; a defeat that returns a valid-but-different result sits outside any bounded enumeration by construction.

WHEN writing a finding DO name the defect class it belongs to, especially if it matches the class the feature under review exists to close — severity alone doesn't convey that; the class-match sets lead-tier rank.

WHEN sweeping a deletion feature for removed terminology DO scan the whole repo, not just diff-touched files — a diff-scoped sweep can pass while live surfaces outside it (commands, docs, injected Expertise) still carry the term.
